history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration revise the basis for apportionment of the after-service health insurance liability between the financial statements of the operations of the United Nations as reported in volume I and in volume II (peacekeeping) to reflect the current ratio of employees and thus the appropriate share of employee benefit liabilities on account of after-service health insurance.
history.administration_response: This recommendation was fully implemented and the Administration requests its closure. A special review of historical records of retirees contained in Umoja as well as in the legacy system was carried out and a new apportionment ratio was established and applied in the actuarial valuation as at 31 December 2021, as follows: 69 per cent of liability was attributed to the regular budget, 14 per cent was attributed to extrabudgetary funding and 17 per cent to volume II (peacekeeping). The new ratio replaced the previously used ratio of 77 per cent attributed to the regular budget, 8 per cent to extrabudgetary funding and 15 per cent to peacekeeping. The impact of this change on the after-service health insurance liability reported in the financial statements of the operations of the United Nations (volume I) for the year ended 31 December 2021 was a decrease of approximately $58 million. The matter was discussed with the Board in detail and the notes to the financial statements of volume I for the year ended 31 December 2021 were revised to include a description of this change and its impact on the financial statements.
history.board_assessment: Given that a special review of historical records of retirees contained in Umoja as well as in the legacy system was carried out and a new apportionment ratio was established and applied in the actuarial valuation as at 31 December 2021, the Board considers this recommendation implemented.
